transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-28
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Sofia Ramos (Redwood SE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Redwood CSM), Priya Shah (NovoHealth Eng Lead), Marcus Lin (NovoHealth Platform), Alicia Gomez (NovoHealth CTO), Tom Harris (NovoHealth SRE)

Summary:
Quick alignment on the benchmark onramp for the POC. Primary goals: validate customer-provided inference scripts against Redwood's harness, decide streaming vs non-streaming mode for production-like load, and define SLA/acceptance criteria for throughput/latency/cost. Agreed next steps and owners; Redwood to run a dry-run and share results.

Topics:
- Customer script shape and variability (token lengths, streaming yields)
- Workload sizing: qps, concurrency, tail latency targets
- Harness integration points: auth, input adapters, KV/prefix caching, streaming fallback
- Metrics to capture: p50/p90/p99 latencies, token rate, error rate, cost per 1k tokens
- Timeline and acceptance criteria for POC signoff

Action items (repeated in metadata): see action_items field

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: All right, thanks everyone for hopping on. Uh, quick roll call — I see Priya, Marcus, Alicia, Tom — hey — and on the Redwood side Sofia, Ethan and Maya, thanks. The plan for 45-ish minutes is to align on the harness onramp and what you want us to validate in the dry-run.

[00:18] Priya Shah: Yeah hi, thanks. I'll keep it short. We're mainly trying to validate our customer-side script that orchestrates prompts and post-processes outputs. We have conversational and single-turn workloads; conversational uses streaming extensively. We need to know if streaming introduces unacceptable tail latency under our target throughput.

[00:37] Sofia Ramos: Got it. Could you describe the script -- like, is it opening a persistent connection per user, does it reuse connections, how do you chunk prompts?

[00:45] Priya Shah: Right, so our web tier reuses a connection pool, we do chunking at sentence boundaries, and for convo state we keep a K-V — key value — cache locally in the service. The harness would need the same prefix/context semantics so tokens line up.

[01:05] Marcus Lin: One nuance: some flows are batch-burst where we fan out to 50 workers, others are single user low-latency. The POC should cover both because the cost math is different.

[01:18] Ethan Park: Okay, this is great. I want to call out two integration patterns we typically see: streaming-first (persistent stream per request) vs request-response (non-streaming). Streaming has better per-req perceived latency but can increase CPU work and may hit tail latency on cold starts. Non-streaming is easier for batching and higher throughput.

[01:40] Priya Shah: Yeah, and we have a specific SLA target: p95 end-to-end under 450 ms for single-turn critical API, and p99 under 900 ms ideally. Is that something you can reproduce in the harness?

[01:52] Sofia Ramos: We'll try. Important to clarify: our measured SLOs at Redwood are typically token-emission latency and model inference latency; end-to-end also includes your pre/post processing. For the dry-run we can run the harness and capture model-side metrics and you can run your side to capture end-to-end; then we'll correlate traces.

[02:12] Tom Harris: On the infra side, we need to confirm network egress and VPC peering. We don't want customer data traversing public internet. Do you support private peering or a bastion?

[02:22] Jordan Lee: Yes — for Dedicated and Private we support VPC peering and private endpoints. For the hosted dry-run we can do a temporary secure tunnel, but for production you'll want dedicated/private. We'll note that as a checklist item.

[02:34] Alicia Gomez: Also can you run the harness with quantized model variants? We want to see cost/quality tradeoffs and maybe route lower-priority requests to quantized models.

[02:45] Sofia Ramos: Absolutely — we can run the same script against a fp16 variant and an int8-ish quantized profile. We'll return quality metrics (like perplexity / output diffs) and token cost. If you have a quality rubric, please share it — that'll help us pick thresholds.

[03:02] Priya Shah: We'll share a small set of 25 golden prompts + expected outputs. Some will be open-ended, so we'll give fuzzy-matching rules.

[03:12] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Let's talk workload sizing — what target QPS and concurrency should we configure for the harness?

[03:18] Marcus Lin: For baseline: 200 RPS single-turn, 40 concurrent streaming sessions for conversational peak. Burst to 500 RPS for scheduled batch jobs. These are initial numbers; if the harness reveals different bottlenecks we'll iterate.

[03:34] Ethan Park: Quick note, streaming concurrency and RPS interact with batching very differently. If you try to force high batching with streaming, you'll see higher per-request latency. For the dry-run we'll run three profiles: low-latency (200 RPS, minimal batching), throughput (batching tuned for tokens/sec), and conversational (40 persistent streams).

[03:55] Priya Shah: Sounds good. How will you verify tail latencies? We need p99 visibility across retries and cold starts.

[04:02] Sofia Ramos: We'll capture p50/p90/p99 at both model side and harness client side. There may be small transcription noise — like, our logs sometimes record "cold start" events as "coldstar" — but we'll include traces. We'll also provide raw samples for any outliers.

[04:20] Priya Shah: One more thing — our script occasionally does a short-circuit: if the model emits a specific token we stop early. Will the harness support early termination in streaming?

[04:29] Ethan Park: Yes, we can simulate early SSE close or send the termination marker. We'll need the exact token or condition to match. Add that to the sample scripts.

[04:40] Jordan Lee: Let's cover quality/acceptance. Priya mentioned a small golden set. What are pass/fail criteria?

[04:47] Priya Shah: For now, pass if exact-match rate >= 70% on deterministic prompts, and fuzzy similarity score > 0.75 on open prompts. Also no more than 0.5% error rate (502/5xx) during the run.

[04:58] Sofia Ramos: That's reasonable. We'll compute similarity using BLEU and a simple embedding cosine if you supply examples. We'll flag any hallucinations.

[05:10] Marcus Lin: Cost is also an acceptance axis — we don't want 3x cost on production traffic for minor latency gains. Can Redwood provide estimated $/1K tokens for the profiles?

[05:19] Jordan Lee: Yes, as part of the dry-run deliverable we'll include estimated token cost and a sensitivity table across batching/quantization choices.

[05:28] Alicia Gomez: Regarding the harness adapter: our script is Python-based using our internal client with a JSON envelope. Will you accept a simple adapter shim, or do we need to rewrite?

[05:37] Sofia Ramos: We can accept a shim. Best practice is a thin adapter that maps your JSON envelope to the Redwood harness format. If you can drop a Python file and a small wrapper, our SEs will wire it in.

[05:48] Priya Shah: Good. We have a small internal SDK — we'll produce a sample shim.

[05:55] Jordan Lee: On the timeline side: everyone okay with Redwood doing a dry-run by next Tuesday (2026-06-02), and then a sync to review on Thursday (2026-06-04)?

[06:03] Marcus Lin: That works. We need to ensure the sample dataset is uploaded to the shared S3 before the run.

[06:10] Tom Harris: Regarding security docs — we need SOC2 + encryption-at-rest details to be part of the package. Can you share that?

[06:17] Maya Singh: I'll attach a redacted SOC 2 summary and KMS/HSM details to the Confluence page. We'll also include network diagrams for the peering test.

[06:26] Priya Shah: Great. Back to streaming vs non-streaming: do you have a recommended default for a hybrid routing policy? We want low-latency for critical single-turns and cheaper quantized routes for background summarization.

[06:36] Sofia Ramos: We often recommend a tiered routing policy: route critical single-turn to low-latency serving group (dedicated capacity, fewer tokens per batch), route background to quantized instances with higher batching. Redwood's routing can do percentage splits and fallback policies if the primary is constrained. We'll propose a config for that.

[06:53] Priya Shah: Are there gotchas around KV cache consistency across replicas? Our convo context must be consistent in order.

[07:01] Ethan Park: Good question. For stateful convo we recommend pinning sessions to a serving shard or using a centralized session store that the harness reads for the dry-run. We'll document a couple options and tradeoffs.

[07:12] Priya Shah: Cool. Anything else on observability? We want token-level cost breakouts and per-route traces.

[07:18] Jordan Lee: That's in Redwood Console — we'll export per-route metrics and token cost, plus traces. For the POC we'll give a 7-day retention snapshot for the trial.

[07:26] Alicia Gomez: Could you include a small CSV that maps prompt types to expected token consumption? That helps us forecast billings.

[07:32] Sofia Ramos: We'll generate that from the dry-run and include the sensitivity matrix.

[07:40] Priya Shah: Quick side note — we use SAML SSO, so when we move to private we'll want SSO integrations. Not urgent for the dry-run but wanted a note.

[07:48] Maya Singh: Noted, Priya. We'll capture SSO and RBAC items in the security checklist.

[07:55] Jordan Lee: All right, let's recap next steps and owners. Sofia to run dry-run against customer script once Priya uploads artifact. Jordan to share benchmark template and cost model. Maya to share SOC2 + network diagram. Priya and Marcus to upload prompts and dataset. We'll sync on 6/4 to review results.

[08:15] Priya Shah: Perfect. Minor transcription noise I noticed in the sample earlier — sometimes "K-V" got transcribed as "Kevin" in our logs, so forgive any weird words in the artifacts.

[08:25] Sofia Ramos: Haha we see that a lot — our auto-transcripts mis-hear acronyms.

[08:30] Ethan Park: One last technical clarification: for the streaming sessions you mentioned 40 concurrency, is that sustained or burst?

[08:36] Marcus Lin: Sustained for typical daytime, spikes to ~90 during onboarding waves. So please model both.

[08:44] Sofia Ramos: We'll add a sustained profile and a spike profile. Also will run an error injection test to see how routing/fallback behaves when we intentionally drop a pod.

[08:55] Priya Shah: That would be great.

[09:00] Jordan Lee: Cool — thanks everyone. We'll send the notes and a Confluence link. Any final questions?

[09:07] Alicia Gomez: No, thank you.

[09:09] Tom Harris: Thanks all.

[09:10] Jordan Lee: End.

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker labels may have been auto-assigned and acronyms sometimes garbled (e.g., "VPC" as "V P C", "KV" as "Kevin"). Where we referenced shared artifacts we put links in the follow-up Confluence page instead of embedding them in the transcript.
